texts: The most common cause for reintervention after the arterial switch is supravalvar pulmonary stenosis: B.
The narrowing forms at the suture line of the reconstructed pulmonary artery, often with branch stretching from the Lecompte maneuver, and is treated with balloon dilation or patch enlargement.
Survival after the arterial switch is excellent, above 90 percent at 10 years, and patients with an intact septum have the lowest mortality.
Rastelli and Nikaidoh repairs, used when there is a VSD with pulmonary stenosis, still need later conduit or outflow reinterventions.
In the picture, after the switch an iron clamp pinches the money pipe just above its sewn door.
Memory hook: after the switch, the money pipe narrows at its seam.
